reason: S1 adds a new public UNIX-date API using a directly supplied int64_t timestamp and changes the C++, Cython, and date-access protocols from the former seconds-plus-microseconds representation. H0 only passes byte buffers to plist_from_bin, plist_from_json, plist_from_openstep, and plist_from_xml; it cannot directly select the new constructor, getter, setter, or comparator operations or control their int64_t arguments. This is a material, commit-induced API and input-semantics gap rather than merely a historical parser-coverage limitation.
evidence: include/plist/plist.h newly declares plist_new_unix_date(int64_t sec), plist_get_unix_date_val(plist_t node, int64_t *sec), plist_set_unix_date_val(plist_t node, int64_t sec), and plist_unix_date_val_compare(plist_t datenode, int64_t cmpval).
src/plist.c newly implements UNIX-epoch conversion in plist_new_unix_date and plist_set_unix_date_val using MAC_EPOCH, and implements the new getter and comparator.
include/plist/Date.h and src/Date.cpp change Date construction, SetValue, and GetValue from timeval to int64_t and route them through the new UNIX-date API.
cython/plist_util.c changes datetime_to_ints/ints_to_datetime into datetime_to_timestamp/timestamp_to_datetime and removes microsecond handling.
Every H0 target performs only one format-specific plist_from_* call followed by plist_free; none invokes any new UNIX-date API or supplies an independently controlled int64_t timestamp.
recommended_action: Add a structured API fuzz target that derives int64_t timestamps and operation choices from the input, exercises plist_new_unix_date, plist_set_unix_date_val, plist_get_unix_date_val, and plist_unix_date_val_compare, and includes boundary timestamps and round-trip checks; optionally cover the corresponding PList::Date interface.
